purpose: Production objects that legitimately differ from the repo migrations. Each entry names exactly ONE object and pins it to the definitionHash in docs/launch/rc2-3-10b-schema-fingerprint.json, so a later change to the object invalidates the exception.
rules: No wildcards. Entries never use `public.*` or any pattern; one object per entry.
Only drift in the direction PROD_ONLY (production has it, the repo does not) can be an exception, and only with a stated reason, an owner and a disposition.
An object the repo defines and the client calls but production lacks (ABSENT / REPO_ONLY) is a BLOCKER, never an exception. See notExceptions.
An exception does not waive security review: its advisor findings are still classified in docs/launch/rc2-3-10b-security-advisor-classification.json.
A changed definitionHash voids the exception until it is re-reviewed.

exceptions.name: _jev_triage_tmp
exceptions.reason: Leftover scratch table (request_id bigint, feedback_id uuid, 5 rows) from a manual feedback-triage run through pg_net. No reference in src, supabase/migrations, supabase/pending or supabase/functions.
exceptions.risk: LOW. RLS is enabled with no policy, so anon/authenticated are denied; anon/authenticated still hold table-level grants until least-privilege grants are applied. Rows reference feedback ids only (no message text).
exceptions.requiredBefore: PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_READY (export first via OA-DATA-EXPORT, then owner-approved DROP)
exceptions.expiresWhen: table dropped; then delete this entry

exceptions.name: rls_auto_enable
exceptions.reason: Function behind the production event trigger `ensure_rls` (ddl_command_end on CREATE TABLE / CREATE TABLE AS / SELECT INTO, owner postgres, enabled). It turns RLS on for tables created in public. Not defined in any repo migration.
exceptions.risk: LOW and protective: new tables get RLS even if a migration forgets it. Not executable by anon/authenticated (snapshot: anonExecute=false, authenticatedExecute=false).
exceptions.requiredBefore: Before any migration is applied: the apply plan must expect RLS to be auto-enabled on new tables (migrations that rely on RLS being off, or that create tables and then add policies, still work).
exceptions.expiresWhen: Either the guard is captured in a repo migration (preferred, forward migration after reconcile) or removed with owner approval; then delete this entry

exceptions.name: ensure_rls
exceptions.pinnedHashBasis: not-fingerprinted (event triggers are outside the table/view/function fingerprint)
exceptions.reason: Event trigger that calls public.rls_auto_enable() (see EXC-RLS-AUTO-ENABLE-FN). Read from pg_event_trigger on 2026-10-08: evtevent ddl_command_end, evtenabled O.

notExceptions.note: These differences are NOT exceptions. They are blockers or open reconciliation items and must not be added to `exceptions` to turn a gate green.

notExceptions.columnLevelDrift: NOT_RUN. The snapshot is table-level; per-column drift (for example profiles columns added by profiles_social_columns) is unproven either way and is not covered by any exception.
